subject: Re: Data residency & region pinning - follow up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmebank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T15:10:00-04:00
Subject: Data residency / region pinning - recap and next steps

Hi Liam — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Acme Bank requirement: customer data (including PII) must remain in EU region(s) for processing and at-rest storage.
- Need clarification on cross-region failover / DR policy (acceptable failover targets, max RTO/RPO).
- Backups: prefer EU-only backups; confirm retention window and encryption requirements.
- Audit logging & access controls: need audit log retention and proof of segregation for support engineers.

What Redwood can provide (summary):
- Region pinning: we can pin customer traffic and data to EU-only regions (e.g., eu-west-1) for hosted or Dedicated deployments.
- Cross-region failover: configurable routing policies that fail over to a defined secondary region only under outage conditions; failover behavior is policy-driven and can be restricted to EU-only if desired.
- Backups: nightly backups stored in the pinned region by default; we also offer optional geo-redundant backups (configurable) — we will mark these as disabled for EU-only requirements unless you request.
- Encryption & KMS: envelope encryption at rest with support for customer-managed keys (KMS) in Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted supports provider-managed KMS but we can discuss Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise.
- Audit logs & retention: admin/audit logs available via the Console and exportable to your SIEM; configurable retention windows and S3 delivery to a customer-owned bucket for retention beyond default.
- PII handling: options to opt-out of request/response logging and disable telemetry for specific routes to avoid storing sensitive inputs.

Attachments: attached a short architecture diagram (region-pin-arch-diagram.pdf) and a SOC2 snapshot for initial compliance review.

Open items / asks for you: 
1) Confirm whether backups must be strictly EU-only (no geo-replication) or if geo-redundant backups within EU are acceptable.
2) Confirm acceptable secondary regions for DR (EU-only or cross-region allowed).
3) Any specific encryption/KMS constraints (customer KMS required?).

Next steps we propose:
- I can put together a short technical deep-dive (15–30m) with our infra lead to walk the architecture and answer detailed questions — are you available Friday 3 Apr or Monday 6 Apr?
- We’ll follow up with a one-page technical note that answers the three open items above.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Vanessa and Marissa on timing.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: region-pin-arch-diagram.pdf (diagram, 1 page), redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf (summary, 3 pages)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmebank.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-31T09:08:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Data residency / region pinning - recap and next steps

Thanks Aditya — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our security & infra team: 

1) EU-only: We need assurance that *all* customer data (inputs, model state, logs, snapshots, backups) will remain within EU boundaries. We have a strong preference for no outbound replication to non-EU regions.
2) Cross-region failover: For DR we want the ability to fail over within EU (e.g., eu-west-1 -> eu-north-1). If there is a hard requirement for cross-region (non-EU) failover, that would need explicit approval from our compliance team — we'd prefer to avoid that.
3) Backups & retention: Our baseline is 90-day backups stored in EU with immutable snapshots. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports immutable snapshots and S3 object lock for backups delivered to our S3?
4) Logging: We need audit logs retained for 365 days and an export to our Splunk/SIEM. We also need to control whether request/response content is logged; ideally we can disable it for routes handling sensitive PII.
5) KMS: We require customer-managed keys (BYOK) where the key material is in our KMS and access is auditable.

Would be great to get the technical note addressing these items and a short call with the infra team. Friday 3 Apr is tight for us — can we do Monday 6 Apr 10:00 CET instead?

— Liam
Infrastructure Security, Acme Bank
liam.oconnor@acmebank.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmebank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T11:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data residency / region pinning - recap and next steps

Hi Liam — thanks for the detailed list, and great constraints to be explicit about. Answers inline below and a proposed next step. 

1) EU-only data residency: Yes — we support EU-only deployments where processing and at-rest storage are constrained to selected EU regions. For Hosted customers we can pin model endpoints and storage to EU regions and disable any cross-region replication. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can guarantee all data stays within your VPC/regions.

2) Cross-region failover: We support policy-driven failover. If you require EU-only failover, we can restrict secondaries to EU regions only (e.g., eu-west-1 -> eu-north-1). Cross-region (non-EU) failover is supported but only when explicitly enabled in the routing policy and would need contract/SLA sign-off.

3) Backups & immutable snapshots: Nightly backups can be stored in the pinned EU region. We can export backups into your customer-owned S3 bucket. We support S3 Object Lock (governance/compliance modes) for exported backups so immutable snapshots are possible — we'll surface the configuration in the technical note.

4) Logging & retention: Audit logs (admin actions, infrastructure events) are available and can be exported to your SIEM. We can configure 365-day retention and direct S3 exports. Request/response logging is optional per-route and can be disabled for endpoints handling sensitive PII.

5) KMS / BYOK: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we can integrate with your KMS in some enterprise configurations (we'll document trade-offs). Key access is auditable and we can provide key usage logs as part of the compliance package.

Open/unknowns from our side: 
- Do you want backups stored in our default backup vault (we will restrict to EU) or do you prefer deliveries to your S3 with Object Lock controlled by you?
- Do you want to enable cross-region failover at all (even EU-only secondaries), or prefer single-region with manual DR procedures?

Next steps:
- I’ll circulate a 1-page technical note with confirmatory answers and configuration options (attached: region-pin-arch-diagram.pdf).
- Schedule the infra deep-dive for Mon, 6 Apr at 10:00 CET (we'll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

Cc'ing Vanessa and Marissa to coordinate procurement/contract questions and the backup export details.

Best,
Aditya
